deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is part of a letter by Karl Hattendorff, most likely to Heinrich Weber, who was then preparing Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The next folio is dated Aachen, 9 Nov 1875. The letter describes how Riemann's memoir on minimal surfaces, 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', came to be written.

The previous page tells how Riemann, in April 1866, asked Hattendorff through Weber to help write up material he had worked out mentally. Riemann could not speak, so he jotted aphoristic hints on a slate. This page continues:
- Hattendorff wrote up the material in between these sessions, which rarely lasted more than half an hour.
- In this way Riemann saw and approved most of the treatise.
- In June Riemann felt an irresistible longing for Italy and left on 16 June.

Hattendorff then discusses how to present this history publicly in a note to the Werke. He wants to avoid painful allusions to Riemann's last months, out of regard for the family. He proposes the following order:
1. A statement on when the manuscript (M.S.) was written.
2. Possibly the last paragraph of his own introduction, 'salva redactione' (subject to editing).
3. A notice that Weierstrass solved the problem at the same time as Riemann but published only after Riemann's death. Weierstrass's paper appeared in the Berlin Monatsberichte in Oct 1866; Riemann died 20 July 1866. The notice should also say that Hattendorff did not know Weierstrass's paper when his introduction was printed (Riemann's memoir appeared in the Göttingen Abhandlungen 13, 1867).

In the left margin Hattendorff promises to carefully edit the note and send it on in a few days, so as not to delay the letter. He signs 'Ihr ergebenster K. Hattendorff'.

The document matters for the provenance of the minimal-surface memoir and for the Riemann–Weierstrass priority question; it contains no derivations.

results.what: Historical account of how Riemann's minimal-surface memoir was composed: dictated via slate notes to Hattendorff in April–June 1866. Also a proposed editorial note on Weierstrass's simultaneous but later-published solution.
results.modern_name: Provenance and editorial history of Riemann's 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Riemann–Weierstrass representation of minimal surfaces)
results.usually_credited_to: Memoir: Riemann, edited by Hattendorff (1867). Parallel work: Weierstrass (1866). Editorial note: Riemann's Werke (1876, ed. Weber/Dedekind).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an editorial letter by Hattendorff with no mathematical content. Its substance (Hattendorff writing up Riemann's minimal-surface work in 1866, and the note on Weierstrass) is reflected in the published Werke and is well known to historians.
transcription_corrections: Line 3–4: 'in Kürze[?] unverzüglich[?] auf' more likely reads 'im Zusammenhange auf' (broken across the line as 'im Zu-/sammenhange auf').
The interlinear insertion 'die Aufgabe' above 'Riemann ... gelöst' is correctly placed.
